title: Black, White and Read All Over

bands.1:
You have won Chief Editor Krak's badge. Now he is on your side.

"The Edit Bay works all night," he says. "Strike that. At three o'clock, the editors nap. We go in through the old lava tube."

Indi's disguises are newspapers with eyeholes. Mo's is upside down.

"What's black and white and read all over?" asks Mo. "A newspaper!"

Everyone groans. But Krak nods. "I would not change one word."

Gus holds up a jar. "The Eggsplosion! Rotten eggs from under my bunk. That's not gross. That's science."

At three, you creep through the hot lava tube.

The Edit Bay is full of screens. Editors in gold tracksuits snore at their desks. A sign says, "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Creatures sit in cages. Scorchquill is locked in a glass box.

Zed tries MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. He types FLAWLESSME. A drawer opens.

Inside is a gold hard drive: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

Maxx is on his gold jet ski. He throws a net over a tiny Creature, with his own hands.

"Now I rescue it," Maxx says. "Pass the onions."

You take the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages.

"The Reef Rays scored!" squeaks Tully, too loudly.

The editors wake up. Goldies run in.

"TULLY!"

Gus opens the jar. It stinks like volcano gas.

"The volcano is going to blow!" yells a Goldie. They all run.

One Goldie blocks the door. He reads a card. "Do NOT let them leave."

Scorchquill burns a line through NOT.

"Do let them leave," reads the Goldie. He holds the door open.

"They cut my NOT," says Krak. "I cut theirs."

Then you play the last clip. Maxx is on a big yacht.

"The finale is LIVE," he says. "No edits. It has to go perfectly."

"No edits," says Krak. "So if it goes wrong, the whole world sees."
bands.2:
You have won Chief Editor Krak's badge, and now he is on your side.

"The Edit Bay works all night," he says. "Strike that. Except at three o'clock, when the editors nap. We go in through the old lava tube."

Indi's disguises are newspapers with eyeholes cut through the front page. Mo's newspaper is upside down.

"Hey, what's black and white and read all over?" asks Mo. "A newspaper!"

Everyone groans. Krak thinks hard. "Red and read," he says at last. "I would not change one word."

Mo has to sit down. Nobody has ever liked his jokes before.

Gus holds up a taped jar. "The Eggsplosion. Twelve eggs, rotting under my bunk since Easter. That's not gross. That's science."

At three o'clock, the crew creeps through the lava tube.

The Edit Bay is a red-lit room with a wall of glowing screens. Editors in gold tracksuits snore at their desks. A sign says, "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Along the back wall are cages of Nodrakes, Barkindles and a Whetwing. In a fireproof box marked "AUTO-EDITOR (TEST)" sits Scorchquill, her crest feathers glowing dim and sad.

Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. He types FLAWLESSME. A drawer slides open.

Inside is a gold hard drive: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

On the screen, Maxx sits on his gold jet ski, sweating. He throws a gold net over a tiny Creature with his own hands. Then he grins at the camera. "Okay. Now I rescue it. Pass the onions."

"That's the rescue we watched on the day we set sail," says Indi.

"Uncut," says Krak. "Every second. That's the truth."

You pocket the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages.

Tully's radio crackles. "The Reef Rays scored a goal!" she squeaks, too loudly.

Every editor sits up. Goldies pour through the doors.

"TULLY!"

Gus rips open the Eggsplosion. A grey-green stink rolls across the room.

"Volcano gas!" yells a Goldie. "She's going to blow!" Everyone runs.

One Goldie stays, blocking the door. He reads from a card: "Orders from Maxx. Do NOT let them leave."

Scorchquill burns a neat black line through one word.

"Do let them leave," the Goldie reads. He shrugs and holds the door open. "Orders are orders."

"They cut my NOT," says Krak. "So I cut theirs."

Later, you play the last clip. Maxx is on the deck of a huge yacht at night.

"The big finale is LIVE," he says. "No edits. So when I catch THE BIG ONE, it has to go perfectly."

"No edits," says Krak. "Then if anything goes wrong, the whole world sees it."
bands.3:
You have won Chief Editor Krak's badge, and the fiercest editor in the archipelago is finally on your side. He spreads a map of the crater across his desk and circles a spot in red.

"The Edit Bay works all night," he says. "Strike that. It works all night, except at three o'clock, when the editors have a nap. We go in through the old lava tube. Read it back!"

Indi hands out disguises: copies of the Redpen Rumble with eyeholes cut through the front page. Mo's newspaper is upside down.

"Hey, what's black and white and read all over?" asks Mo. "A newspaper!"

Everyone groans. Krak considers it seriously. "Red and read. A pun," he says at last. "And there is not one word I would change."

Mo has to sit down. Nobody has ever approved of anything he's said.

Gus holds up a jar sealed with tape. "The Eggsplosion," he whispers. "Twelve eggs that have been rotting under my bunk since Easter. That's not gross. That's science. Volcano gas smells like rotten eggs too."

At three o'clock, the crew creeps into the lava tube. It is pitch black and hot enough to bake bread.

The tunnel ends at a gold grate. Beyond it lies the Edit Bay, a long red-lit room with a wall of glowing screens. Editors in gold tracksuits snore at their desks. A sign above them reads: "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Along the back wall are cages of Nodrakes, Barkindles and a Whetwing with its wings pinned. In a fireproof glass box marked "AUTO-EDITOR (TEST)" sits Scorchquill, her crest feathers glowing dim and sad.

Zed types MAXXISGREAT into the main desk. Wrong. He types FLAWLESSME. A drawer slides open.

Inside is a gold hard drive: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

On the big screen, Maxx sits on his gold jet ski, red-faced and sweating. He throws a gold net over a tiny Creature with his own hands.

"Ugh, it's looking at me. Throw it again," he snaps. Then he grins at the camera. "Okay. Now I rescue it. Somebody pass the onions."

"That's the rescue we watched on the day we set sail," says Indi. "The one with his logo on the net."

Krak's eyes are shining. "Uncut," he says. "Every word. Every second. That's the truth."

You pocket the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages, and Scorchquill leaps onto Krak's shoulder, blazing red again.

Then Tully's radio crackles. "The Reef Rays scored a goal!" she squeaks, much too loudly.

Every editor sits bolt upright. Goldies pour through the doors.

"TULLY!"

Gus rips the tape off the Eggsplosion. A grey-green stink rolls across the room.

"Volcano gas!" yells a Goldie. "She's going to blow!" Editors and Goldies stampede for the exit.

Only one Goldie stays, blocking the door. He reads from a card: "Orders from Maxx. Do NOT let them leave."

Scorchquill breathes on the card, and a neat black line burns straight through one word.

"Do let them leave," the Goldie reads. He shrugs and holds the door open. "Orders are orders."

"They cut my NOT," says Krak. "So I cut theirs."

Back in the Rumble office, you play the last clip. Maxx is on the deck of a huge yacht at night.

"Note for the big finale," he says. "It's LIVE. No cuts. No edits. So when I catch THE BIG ONE, it has to go perfectly."

Krak leans back slowly, his eyebrows rising like smoke.

"No edits," he says. "Then if anything goes wrong, the whole world sees it."
bands.4:
You have won Chief Editor Krak's badge, and the fiercest editor in the archipelago is finally on your side. He spreads a map of the crater across his desk, weighs it down with a paperweight shaped like a full stop, and circles a spot in red.

"The Edit Bay works all night," he says. "Strike that. It works all night, except at three o'clock, when the editors have a nap. We go in through the old lava tube. Read it back!"

"Three o'clock, lava tube," says Zed. "Stealth mission. Got it."

Indi hands out her disguise of the Chapter: copies of the Redpen Rumble with eyeholes cut through the front page. "Nobody ever looks twice at someone reading a newspaper," she explains. Mo's newspaper is upside down.

"Nobody can tell," says Mo. "Hey, what's black and white and read all over?"

Everyone groans before he can finish.

"A newspaper!" says Mo.

Krak considers it seriously, tapping his giant pen against his chin. "Red and read. A pun," he says at last. "And there is not one word I would change."

Mo has to sit down. Nobody has ever approved of anything he's said, ever.

Gus holds up a jar sealed with three layers of tape. "The Eggsplosion," he whispers. "Twelve eggs that have been rotting under my bunk since Easter. That's not gross. That's science. Volcano gas smells like rotten eggs, so one sniff, and the Goldies will think the volcano is about to blow."

At three o'clock, the crew creeps into the lava tube. It is pitch black and hot enough to bake bread. Snipwing bats flit overhead, listening to their own echoes.

"And then we go left, and then we go right, and then..." Zed whispers.

A Snipwing swoops past his ear. Snip! Zed stops saying "and then".

The tunnel ends at a gold grate. Beyond it lies the Edit Bay, a long red-lit room with a wall of glowing screens. Editors in gold tracksuits are snoring at their desks, headphones on. A sign above them reads: "RULE ONE: IF MAXX LOOKS BAD, CUT IT."

Along the back wall are cages: Nodrakes, Barkindles, a Whetwing with its wings pinned and a Strandle plucking sadly at the bars. In a fireproof glass box marked "AUTO-EDITOR (TEST)" sits Scorchquill, her crest feathers glowing dim and sad.

The main desk has a gold keypad. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Wrong. He types FLAWLESSME. A drawer slides open.

Inside is a gold hard drive with a label: "RAW FOOTAGE. NEVER SHOW ANYONE. (I LOOK SWEATY.)"

Zed plugs it in. On the big screen, Maxx sits on his gold jet ski, red-faced and sweating. A tiny Creature is paddling in the sea in front of him. Maxx throws a gold net over it with his own hands.

"Ugh, it's looking at me. Throw it again," he snaps. Then he grins at the camera. "Okay. Now I rescue it. Somebody pass the onions."

"That's the rescue we watched on the day we set sail," says Indi. "The one with his logo on the net."

Krak's eyes are shining. "Uncut," he says. "Every word. Every second. That's not a story. That's the truth."

You pocket the drive. That's the proof. Wren and Krak open the cages, and Scorchquill leaps onto Krak's shoulder, crest blazing bright red again.

Then the footy radio in Tully's pocket crackles. "The Reef Rays scored a goal!" she squeaks, much too loudly.

Every editor sits bolt upright. Alarms wail. Goldies pour through the doors.

"TULLY!"

Gus rips the tape off the Eggsplosion. A grey-green stink rolls across the room like fog.

"Volcano gas!" yells a Goldie. "She's going to blow!" Editors and Goldies stampede for the exit, holding their noses.

Only one Goldie stays, blocking the door. He reads slowly from a card in his hand: "Orders from Maxx. Do NOT let them leave."

Krak plucks the card from his fingers. Scorchquill breathes on it, and a neat black line burns straight through one word.

"Do let them leave," the Goldie reads. He frowns, shrugs and holds the door open. "Orders are orders."

"They cut my NOT," says Krak, with deep satisfaction. "So I cut theirs."

Outside, the Creatures scatter across the warm black rock, and the Whetwing shoots up into the smoke like a rocket.

Back in the Rumble office, you play the last clip on the drive. Maxx is on the deck of a huge yacht at night, talking to his editors.

"Note for the big finale," he says. "It's LIVE. No cuts. No edits. So when I catch THE BIG ONE, it has to go perfectly."

Krak leans back slowly, his eyebrows rising like smoke.

"Live," he says. "No edits. Then if anything goes wrong, the whole world sees it."
